title: Comprehensive Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement & Revenue Recognition Guidance - 2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Introduction
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's policies and operating procedures for (1) budgeting and forecasting, (2) contracts and legal review, (3) procurement and vendor onboarding, and (4) revenue recognition and billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement owners, hiring managers, and stakeholders who participate in committing spend, negotiating customer contracts, or producing revenue reports.

Scope and Objectives
- Provide a single reference for thresholds, ownership, and cadence across related finance-and-legal processes.
- Reduce cycle time for approvals while maintaining control and compliance.
- Ensure consistent ASC 606-aligned revenue recognition and clear billing practices.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
Overview & cadence
- Annual budget process: led by Finance with input from Product, Engineering, GTM and Ops. Draft budget due October 15; final approvals by the Board by December 15.
- Quarterly reforecast (QRF): reforecast within 10 business days after quarter close (Q+10). Exceptions require CFO approval.

Roles & responsibilities
- Finance (FP&A): owns templates, consolidation, variance analysis, monthly forecasting process.
- Department leads: submit line-item budgets, headcount plans, and capital requests.
- People Ops: provides headcount plan reconciliation and offer cost assumptions.

Templates & assumptions
- Use the master budget template (Finance Drive / Budgeting v5.1). Key assumptions: salary inflation 4% (2026), cloud cost growth 18% YOY, model inference spend growth tied to usage metrics.
- Capital requests > $50k must include ROI/ business case and depreciation schedule.

Approval thresholds
- Department managers: up to $25k OPEX annual commit.
- Director approval: $25k- $250k.
- VP approval: $250k- $1M.
- CFO approval: > $1M.

Variance monitoring
- Finance will flag variances >5% monthly and >10% quarter-to-date. Owners must provide remediation plans within 7 business days.

2) Contracts and Legal Review
Contract lifecycle
1. Request & intake: submit contract intake via the contract-management portal (link in Related Pages).
2. Template selection: use approved template that matches transaction type (customer SaaS, reseller, vendor, MSA, SOW).
3. Legal review: standard SLA - 3 business days for template-based agreements, 7-10 business days for negotiated deals.
4. Signing: follow signature authority matrix below.
5. Contract storage: executed contracts must be uploaded to Contract Repository (DocStore) within 24 hours.

Signature authority
- Individual contributors: none.
- Managers: up to $50k for standard vendor agreements (no material risk).
- Directors: up to $250k.
- VP: up to $1M.
- CFO/CEO: >$1M and any agreement that (a) contains carve-outs to IP or (b) creates material indemnity/limitation exposures.

Standard clauses & redlines
- Data processing addendum (DPA) must be attached for any customer/vendor handling customer data.
- Indemnity caps limited to the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $250k, unless escalated.
- No unilateral source-code escrow without Legal approval.

Escalation & timelines
- If counterparty proposes non-standard liability or security terms, route to Legal and Security for joint review. Escalation to GC required for material changes.

3) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding
Procurement workflow
- Low-value purchases (<$2,500): P-Card or designated petty cash with receipts submitted within 7 days.
- Standard PO flow (>$2,500): Requisition -> Purchasing -> PO issuance -> Goods/Services -> Invoice -> AP payment.
- RFP required for engagements expected to exceed $50k annually or for strategic services (e.g., large cloud partners, infrastructure vendors).

Competitive sourcing
- For purchases between $10k- $50k: obtain 3 competitive quotes where feasible and document selection rationale.

Vendor due diligence
- All new vendors must complete Vendor Onboarding questionnaire: business info, AML/KYC (if applicable), security posture (SOC2 or equivalent preferred), and insurance certificates.
- Security review required for vendors accessing production, customer data, or internal systems (owning team must submit Security Intake form).

Payment terms & PO controls
- Standard payment terms: Net 30. Exceptions require Treasury approval.
- Early payment or discounts: Finance to evaluate on a case-by-case basis, maximize cash efficiency.

Ownership & SLAs
- Procurement owns the PO and vendor master record.
- Requesting team owns statement of work, acceptance criteria, and escalation during delivery.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy
Revenue recognition principles
- Redwood follows ASC 606: recognize revenue when control of promised goods/services is transferred in an amount that reflects the consideration expected.
- Common arrangements:
  - Hosted API (usage-based): recognize as usage occurs (variable consideration); apply expected-value or most-likely amount method for estimates; update estimates each reporting period.
  - Annual committed Dedicated/Private contracts: recognize ratably over the contract term unless performance obligations dictate otherwise.
  - One-time professional services (SOW): recognize over time if customer obtains and uses building output; otherwise recognize at completion.

Deferred revenue & billing
- Invoices billed in advance for subscription fees are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized over the term.
- Billing cadence: default monthly in arrears for usage; annual or quarterly in advance for committed capacity if contract specifies.
- Credit memos: issued for billing disputes; disputes >$5k require Finance + Billing investigation and Legal involvement.

Tax & remittance
- Sales tax/VAT: Billing system will calculate based on customer location and tax status. Tax exemptions must be supported by documentation.
- Withholding tax for cross-border contracts handled per jurisdiction; Finance will coordinate with external tax counsel for non-standard arrangements.

Chart of accounts & reporting
- Map revenues to product lines: Hosted API revenue, Dedicated contracts, Professional Services, and Other (credits/adjustments).
- Monthly close checklist includes deferred revenue rollforward, unbilled receivables, and contract liability reconciliation.

Billing operations & disputes
- Billing team SLA: respond to customer billing inquiries within 2 business days; resolve disputes within 15 business days if possible.
- Late payment terms: interest at 1.5% per month after Net terms unless otherwise agreed.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Approval matrix (quick reference)
- Appendix B: Template list and storage locations
- Appendix C: Sample Journal entries for common transactions (sample debit/credit lines)

Change control & review cadence
- This guidance is owned by Finance (FP&A) and Legal. Major updates should be reviewed annually; interim updates require owner sign-off and communication to the company.
